questions.prompt: Operator o has add list {p, q} and delete list {q}. Applying it makes q:
options: True: deletes are applied first and then adds, so q is re-added
Undefined: an operator may not list the same atom in both lists
Unknown: the planner cannot tell without knowing the order of effects
False: the delete list always removes the atom after the add list
questions.explanation: Delete is applied before add, so q ends in the state.

questions.prompt: State {a, b, c}. Operator pre {a, d}. Applicable?
options: Yes, provided that b is true in the state as well
No, because precondition d is missing from the state
Yes, because most of the preconditions are true in the state
Only after a previous step adds d to the state

questions.prompt: State {x,y}. Op: pre {x}, add {z}, delete {x}. Result?
options: {y}: the add list is ignored when an atom is deleted
{y, z}: x is deleted, y is untouched, and z is added
{z}: only the added atom remains afterwards
{x, y, z}: deleting x has no effect once z is added

questions.prompt: 3 locations, 3 objects, capacity one per location, all on the table. How many ways to place the objects (different locations)?
4 locations, 2 objects on the table at different locations, robot at any of the 4 places, hand empty. Number of states?
4 locations, 2 objects, robot holds one (2 choices), the other at one of the 4 locations, robot at one of 4 places. Number of states?
A relaxed reachable set contains the goal. The conclusion:
options: The goal is certainly reachable, so a plan must exist
The goal is certainly unreachable in the real problem
The goal might be reachable; run a full search to find out
The plan has length zero, since the goal is already true
questions.explanation: The relaxation is optimistic; it cannot prove feasibility.

questions.prompt: Heuristic h = number of unsatisfied goal facts. State holds cup at C with free(C); goal {at(cup,C), handempty}. h = ? (true remaining cost is 1)
questions.explanation: Both facts are false, so h=2 > 1: inadmissible.

questions.prompt: Which model feature prevents two objects from being placed on the same location?
options: The move operator, because it moves only one object each time
The goal, which forbids having two objects at one place
The initial state only, since it starts with distinct places
A free(l) precondition that place deletes when it is applied
questions.explanation: Capacity is expressed as a consumable fact.

questions.prompt: A plan is returned. Which check is the most direct validation?
options: Run it twice and see that the result comes out the same both times
Check its length against the shortest plan found by any earlier search
Execute it operator by operator, checking preconditions and the goal
Check that it uses all of the objects that appear in the problem
questions.explanation: Symbolic simulation of the plan checks every step.

questions.prompt: Explain why the delete relaxation is sound for proving impossibility but cannot prove possibility.
rubric: Relaxed reachable facts contain every real reachable fact (induction).
So a fact outside the set is unreachable.
A fact inside may still be blocked by deletes, e.g. a single gripper.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: Describe how you would check a symbolic pick-and-place model against reality before using it on a robot.
rubric: Execute plans in a simulator and compare the symbolic and physical outcomes.
Test each operator's precondition and effect on its own with the real skill (E04).
List constraints the model omits (geometry, collisions) and add tests for them.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
